verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew returned to Earth on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'return to Earth set for Friday, April 10'; R2: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT ... Friday'; R3: 'splashdown of NASA's Artemis 2 astronauts at 8:07 p.m. EDT ... April 10'; R4: 'splashdown on Friday evening (April 10)'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state splashdown/return on April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown ... off the coast of San Diego'; R2: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: All sources directly confirm exact location.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown around 8:07 p.m. (5:07 p.m. PDT) Friday, April 10'; R2: 'splashdown ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and time zones stated verbatim in sources.

verifications.claim: The date of the Artemis II return was Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'return to Earth set for Friday, April 10'; R3: 'splashdown ... April 10, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify Friday, April 10, 2026 as return/splashdown date.

verifications.claim: The location of the Artemis II return was the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'off the coast of San Diego'; R2: 'Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R7: 'off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Consistent description across sources matches claim precisely.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission duration was 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'approximate 10-day mission'; R3: '10-day mission' (multiple); R4: '10-day mission'; R8: '10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources repeatedly describe as 10-day mission, though precise elapsed time is 9 days+; common nominal duration.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission launched on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement in R3 confirms launch date.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft completed the Artemis II mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion’s re-entry and splashdown'; R2: 'Orion spacecraft is back on Earth'; R3: 'NASA’s Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: All sources identify Orion as the spacecraft that flew and returned from Artemis II.

verifications.claim: Recovery teams from the USS John P. Murtha secured the capsule and crew shortly after the Artemis II landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'flown to the USS John P. Murtha. Recovery teams will retrieve the crew'; R2: 'secured in the well deck of USS John P. Murtha'; R3: 'safely aboard the USS John P. Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm USS John P. Murtha as recovery ship securing crew/capsule post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consisted of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and CSA ... Jeremy Hansen'; R2: identical
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew list and affiliations stated verbatim.

verifications.claim: Artemis II was the first crewed mission to the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'first crewed mission to the Moon since 1972'; R4: 'first time in over 53 years'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state it as first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972.
